images.title: Squaring doubles the end zeros
images.purpose: Shows 3000 × 3000 = 9000000: three zeros from each factor give six zeros at the end of the square.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One line of multiplication across the upper middle and its result centred below it.
images.exact_structure: Top line: 3000 × 3000 in large dark digits, the three zeros of the first 3000 coloured teal (#0072B2) and the three zeros of the second 3000 coloured amber (#E69F00). Below, centred: the result 9000000, written with the 9 in dark text, then three teal zeros, then three amber zeros, exactly 6 zeros. A short dark brace under the six zeros is tagged 6 zeros. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A square always ends in twice as many zeros as the number, so an even number of zeros.
images.description: Shows 3000 × 3000 = 9000000: three zeros from each factor give six zeros at the end of the square.

image_decisions.why: Colouring each factor's zeros shows exactly where the doubled zeros come from.
